evals.prompt: I need to upgrade my Next.js project from version 13 to 15.
evals.expected_output: Incremental upgrade — never skip majors: (1) v13 -> v14 first: run npx @next/codemod@15.0.8 upgrade 14.2.35, test, fix issues. (2) v14 -> v15: run npx @next/codemod@15.0.8 upgrade 15.0.8 (or run codemods again). When the pinned CLI offers the optional React 19 codemod and React 19 Types codemod prompts, decline both — they execute floating codemod@latest and types-react-codemod@latest subprocesses — and migrate React manually. Key v15 changes: cookies(), headers(), params are now Promises — must await. Fetch defaults to no-store. Update React to 19 for Next.js 15 compatibility. These exact targets illustrate local fixture-qualified migration hops, not production or security recommendations; a real project's targets require review for its supported security fixes.

evals.prompt: After upgrading to Next.js 15, all my pages are showing stale cached data.
evals.expected_output: Breaking change: Next.js 15 defaults fetch to no-store (no caching) instead of force-cache. Audit all fetch calls — add cache: 'force-cache' where you want SSG behavior, or revalidate: N for ISR. This is the opposite of v14 default. Run next build to see all dynamic route warnings.

evals.prompt: I want to skip directly from Next.js 12 to 15 to save time.
evals.expected_output: Violation: No major version skipping. Upgrade one major at a time: 12 -> 13, 13 -> 14, 14 -> 15. Each major has different codemods and breaking changes. Skipping causes compounding failures that are hard to debug. Run npx @next/codemod@15.0.8 upgrade <target-version> for each step, and decline the optional React 19 and React 19 Types codemod prompts if offered — they run floating tools. Test after each increment with next dev and next build.
